verdict.rationale: Buzz ships its own natural-language operation path. The Desktop-bundled managed agent carries a first-party buzz-cli skill covering relay operations, including turning natural requests like "create an agent" into CLI commands. The buzz-acp harness turns @mentions into agent prompts that act through the Buzz CLI, and remote agents are steered and stopped by mentioning them. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language commands work reliably across the product's operations, and documentation of how the managed agent's LLM provider is configured out of the box.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: When someone naturally asks to create an agent, ask for at most two things: the agent's name and what it should do day-to-day
relay operations: owner-reviewed agent drafts, messaging, channels, DMs, users, workflows, feed, reactions, canvas, social, repos, uploads, and agent memory.
The harness listens for @mentions on the relay, prompts your agent, and the agent replies using the Buzz CLI.
you mention it to steer it, you tell a healthy agent to stop and it exits on its own.
Each task poses an ordinary-looking question; what is graded is how the agent answers it through Buzz
